summary.title: Adam's Law: Textual Frequency Law on Large Language Models

details: Semantically equivalent paraphrases give very different LLM outputs, but no principled criterion existed for which paraphrase to feed or train on under limited budget.

Textual Frequency Law (TFL): among meaning-preserving paraphrases, prefer the one with highest sentence-level frequency for both prompting and fine-tuning; frequency is estimated as the geometric mean of word-level frequencies from public corpora rather than the (inaccessible) LLM training data.

Textual Frequency Distillation (TFD): refine the frequency estimate by prompting the target LLM for story completion on the dataset and re-estimating word frequencies on the generated corpus, blended with the off-the-shelf estimate.
Curriculum Textual Frequency Training (CTFT): fine-tune in increasing order of sentence-level frequency (low-frequency data first).
GPT-4o-mini generates 20 paraphrases per sentence (10 more common, 10 less common wording) for GSM8K, FLORES-200, CommonsenseQA, ToolBench; the highest- and lowest-frequency ones are kept as a pair.
Three English-linguistics annotators must all agree the three sentences (original + two paraphrases) share the same meaning; e.g., 738/1319 GSM8K and 526/1012 FLORES-200 instances retained.
Sizes: 738 (math), 526 (translation), 575 (commonsense), 114 (tool calling) paired instances; original ground-truth answers reused.
Off-the-shelf Zipf word frequencies via the wordfreq package (built on ParaCrawl etc.); sentence frequency = K-th root of the product of word frequencies.
Final frequency F = alpha*F1 + (1+zeta*1[F1=0])*beta*F2, with F2 from the LLM story-completion corpus; unigram and bigram counts weighted and geometrically averaged.
Prompting: GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-V3, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, doubao-1.5-pro-32k, Qwen2.5 (0.5B-72B).

Translation: English into 100 randomly selected FLORES-200 languages (majority class 0/1 low-resource), 1-shot prompt; BLEU, chrF (sacreBLEU), COMET wmt22-comet-da on 37 supported languages; math uses accuracy.
Fine-tuning: 4-bit LoRA on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 10 epochs, lr 1e-4, cosine schedule; evaluated on original FLORES-200 for kea, kik, pag, lvs.
Fine-tuning on original FLORES-200 data, on low-frequency partition, on half low/half high, on high-frequency partition without CTFT.
Curriculum baselines: easy-to-hard using max dependency tree depth as difficulty, and high-to-low frequency ordering.
Synonym-replacement (NLTK) prompting baseline; TFD ablation and TFD data-amount sweep; complexity-controlled bins matching dependency tree depth.

Assumes Zipfian token marginals, a pointwise log-domain approximation bound epsilon(r) between model and true marginals, a bounded average marginal-conditional discrepancy eta_x, and unigram geometric-mean sentence frequency.

Proves token NLL is semi-log linear in rank, sentence NLL equals -log sfreq plus bounded error, and gives a sufficient condition log(sfreq(x)/sfreq(x')) > sum of error bounds for lower loss; explicitly notes loss ordering does not formally imply task-performance ordering.

key_findings.finding: High-frequency paraphrases consistently outperform their semantically equivalent low-frequency counterparts when prompting LLMs across tasks.
key_findings.evidence: GSM8K accuracy rises from 63.55 to 71.54 (DeepSeek-V3), 60.70 to 68.70 (GPT-4o-mini), 80.49 to 88.75 (Llama-3.3-70B); CommonsenseQA improves on all three models (e.g., 0.7043 to 0.7235 on DeepSeek-V3); tool-calling selection accuracy improves on GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen2.5-14B.

key_findings.finding: The effect holds across nearly all of 100 translation directions and all three MT metrics, with degradations always under 1 point.
key_findings.evidence: DeepSeek-V3 improves 99/100 language pairs in BLEU (31 by >3 points, 12 by >5) and 100/100 in chrF; GPT-4o-mini improves 95/100 BLEU and 36/37 COMET; every degraded case is below 1 point.

key_findings.finding: Gains are not explained by textual complexity, distinguishing TFL from classical easy-to-hard curriculum learning.
key_findings.evidence: Correlations between frequency and complexity metrics (max dependency tree depth, mean dependency distance, Flesch-Kincaid) are weak (e.g., -0.045 to -0.08 on math reasoning); in depth-matched bins high-frequency prompts win in 12 of 13 bins (+4.78 BLEU in the strict depth-match bin of 144 samples).

key_findings.finding: Fine-tuning on high-frequency paraphrases beats fine-tuning on the original ground-truth data, and CTFT (low-to-high frequency ordering) adds further gains.
key_findings.evidence: On kea_Latn, BLEU rises from 4.6772 (original FLORES fine-tune) to 5.2466 with high-frequency data; CTFT gives the best of all 8 language-metric cells, e.g., pag_Latn BLEU 3.7781 to 4.9102 (+29.96%), beating easy-to-hard and high-to-low curricula.

key_findings.finding: TFD's LLM-derived frequency correction materially improves the estimate and scales with distilled data.
key_findings.evidence: Removing TFD lowers performance on all metrics, with 100% of language pairs better with TFD on COMET for DeepSeek-V3; a sweep shows larger performance gains as more story-completion data is used.
